blogs.title: Recurrent Unilateral Effusion in a Child: Don't Forget the Pancreas
blogs.description: In children with large, recurrent, blood-stained pleural effusions and few systemic signs, the culprit may be pancreatic. Using this case as a springboard, we outline a rapid bedside approach: re-ask about handlebar or blunt abdominal trauma, order pleural amylase/lipase early, and pivot to abdominal imaging when values are high. We highlight how PPF wears a pulmonary mask and how to avoid prolonged, lung-focused detours.

blogs.title: Why the Right Chest? Anatomy of a Pancreatopleural Fistula
blogs.description: PPF is usually taught as a left-sided entity, but posterior duct or pseudocyst leaks can track retroperitoneally through the esophageal hiatus into the right pleural space—and even communicate bilaterally. This post dissects the anatomic highways that explain right-greater-than-left effusions, showing how laterality should not reassure clinicians away from a pancreatic source.

blogs.title: CT, MRCP, then ERCP: Imaging the Invisible Duct in Paediatric PPF
blogs.description: What to order and when: CT can reveal pseudocysts and retroperitoneal tracks but often misses the fistula; MRCP boosts visualization of the duct and fistulous tract (roughly 70%–80% sensitivity), and ERCP remains the gold standard for therapeutic planning. We propose a pragmatic, time-saving pathway that balances sensitivity, radiation, and sedation considerations in children with suspected PPF.

blogs.title: Octreotide, NPO, and a Tube: Making Conservative Therapy Work
blogs.description: Conservative care still matters: bowel rest, TPN, chest drainage, pancreatic enzyme replacement, and a somatostatin analogue (e.g., octreotide 10–40 mcg/kg/day) can quiet the leak. We discuss what to monitor (daily drain output, nutritional markers), the expected response window (about 10–21 days), and how to optimize success while recognizing that pediatric closure rates are modest and timely escalation may be needed.

blogs.title: When to Stent, When to Cut: A Step-Up Strategy for Paediatric PPF
blogs.description: When drainage and octreotide fail or a ductal stenosis is evident, ERCP with transpapillary stenting can rapidly decompress the duct and close the fistula, with high reported success in children. We outline decision points for early endoscopy versus surgery (distal pancreatectomy, Puestow, cystojejunostomy), expected timelines to closure, stent dwell times, and outcomes to guide escalation.

blogs.title: ADA Isn't TB: Interpreting Hemorrhagic Effusions Without Anchoring
blogs.description: Mildly elevated pleural ADA is nonspecific and can rise with diverse inflammatory states; in a hemorrhagic effusion it should not trigger empiric anti-TB without corroboration. We contrast the low yield of anchoring on ADA with the high discriminative value of pleural amylase/lipase (and amylase isoenzyme typing) for PPF, and suggest a simple rule-in/rule-out sequence to avoid misdiagnosis in high-TB settings.
